title: Attorney General of Wisconsin

context.text: The race is a rematch of 2022, when Kaul narrowly defeated Toney.

summary.text: Josh Kaul is the incumbent Democratic Attorney General of Wisconsin, seeking a third term in a rematch with Republican Eric Toney, whom he narrowly defeated in 2022. A former federal prosecutor, he took office in January 2019. His campaign centers on public safety; his office has also joined more than 60 lawsuits against the Trump administration and brought the suit over Wisconsin's 1849 abortion law.

background.text: Grew up in Oshkosh and Fond du Lac; a former federal prosecutor.
Sworn in as Wisconsin's 45th Attorney General on January 7, 2019; has won twice by less than a percentage point, per PBS Wisconsin.

priorities.text: Public safety, which he calls his top priority as Attorney General, including requests to the Legislature for more positions at the state crime laboratories.
Challenging federal actions: he says his office has won "case after case" in lawsuits that keep federal funds from being frozen or conditioned.

statements.quote: I had filed a lawsuit seeking to block enforcement of a law that dates back to the mid-1800s.
statements.context: In an October 2026 PBS Wisconsin interview, about his lawsuit over the 1849 law; the Wisconsin Supreme Court overturned the law in July 2025, per PBS

record.text: Joined a first lawsuit against the Trump administration on January 21, 2025, challenging an executive order on birthright citizenship, and has since joined more than 60 such lawsuits, many over federal funding cuts, per PBS Wisconsin.

Filed a lawsuit seeking to block enforcement of Wisconsin's 1849 abortion law; the Wisconsin Supreme Court overturned the law in a decision issued in July 2025, leaving a 20-week limit in place, per PBS Wisconsin.

Requested 19 additional crime-laboratory positions in the 2025 state budget; the Legislature's Joint Finance Committee provided none. In 2023 he had sought 16, and the Legislature approved 3, per PBS Wisconsin. Toney says a nonpartisan audit found positions went unfilled and DNA testing slowed; Kaul says the shortfall reflects the Legislature's funding decisions.

Wisconsin DOJ joined a coalition suing in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York to halt the Trump administration's new public charge rule, announced September 14, 2026; Kaul is quoted in the release.

Wisconsin DOJ announced on September 21, 2026 that Wisconsin joined a $694 million multistate settlement with Credit Acceptance Corporation; Wisconsin is to receive an estimated $218,319, per the release.

candidates.name: Eric Toney
candidates.ballotNote: Republican nominee; also the party's 2022 nominee for this office.
candidates.currentRole: Fond du Lac County District Attorney (since 2013)

summary.text: Eric Toney is the Republican nominee for Attorney General and the Fond du Lac County District Attorney. He lost narrowly to Josh Kaul in 2022 and is running again on a public-safety message focused on the state crime laboratories, fentanyl and what he calls the partisanship of the current Attorney General.

background.text: District Attorney of Fond du Lac County since 2013; past president of the Wisconsin District Attorneys Association and named Wisconsin's 2024 District Attorney of the Year, per his campaign.
Earned degrees in history and political science from St. Norbert College and a law degree from Hamline University.
Was the Republican nominee for Attorney General in 2022, losing narrowly to Josh Kaul.

priorities.text: Fixing delays at the Wisconsin State Crime Laboratories: his campaign says he would end hiring freezes, fill vacancies, and set timelines and performance metrics.

A plan to have state assistant attorneys general serve as Special Assistant U.S. Attorneys, so they can help prosecute gun, drug, human-trafficking and child-exploitation cases in federal court in Milwaukee County and around the state.
Fighting violent crime and supporting law enforcement, per his campaign site.
Addressing the fentanyl epidemic and what he describes as the partisanship of the current Attorney General.

statements.quote: I have not and am not advocating for any changes to the law in Wisconsin
statements.context: In an October 2026 PBS Wisconsin interview, about the 20-week limit that applies after the 1849 law was overturned

record.text: In spring 2023, after the 2022 race, joined Josh Kaul in urging the Republican-controlled Legislature to fund 16 additional crime-laboratory positions; the Legislature approved 3, per PBS Wisconsin.

Kaul's record items now rest on Wisconsin DOJ press-release PDFs (wisdoj.gov). Neither candidate's own words take a side on a listed issue; their abortion remarks are shown as statements.
